c.tagline: Dhow-filled bay town of coconut palms, gateway to Tofo and Barra's whale sharks and manta rays.

taxi.fareNote: There are no ride-hail apps in Inhambane — tuk-tuks and shared chapas (minibuses) handle short hops and the run out to Tofo and Barra; agree the fare with the driver before setting off.

emergency.note: 112 works from mobile phones and connects to emergency services; landline numbers are 119 (police), 117 (ambulance) and 198 (fire).

avoid.reason: Avoid walking Tofo and Barra beaches alone after dark and don't leave belongings unattended — opportunistic theft is the main risk.

hood_desc: The compact historic centre on the bay, with the twin-spired Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, an old waterfront mosque, faded Portuguese-era shophouses, the jetty and market; the walkable base for exploring the town's colonial and dhow heritage.

The famous surf-and-dive beach 22 km east, a long stretch of powdery sand backed by dune bars, dive centres and seafood shacks; the lively, social base for whale-shark and manta diving and Inhambane's nightlife.
A palm-backed sand spit at the peninsula tip with calm, shallow flats, a mangrove estuary and low-key beach lodges; a quieter, family-friendly base for snorkelling, kite-surfing and long walks.
The rocky headland and surf point just south of Tofo, with a sacred cliff, tidal pools and a handful of relaxed lodges; a calmer, scenic alternative to the main Tofo strip.

The busy mainland market town directly across the bay, reached by dhow or ferry, and the region's main transport hub on the EN1 highway; practical rather than touristy, with chapas onward to Maputo and Vilanculos.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap supply is unreliable.

transit.hours: Chapas and tuk-tuks run from around dawn until early evening; after dark, tuk-tuks and pre-arranged taxis are the main way to get around.
transit.note: Inhambane has no formal public transport; getting around means shared chapas (converted minibuses) and tuk-tuks around town and out to the beaches, plus dhows across the bay to Maxixe.
transit.pay: Pay the chapa conductor or tuk-tuk driver in cash (roughly 15-50 meticais a hop; more for Tofo/Barra); dhow crossings are a few meticais. Carry small notes.

bus: Long-distance buses to Maputo & Vilanculos (from Maxixe)
ferry: Dhows and motor ferry across the bay to Maxixe

transit.m: Tuk-tuk or taxi to the town centre (5-10 min)
Chapa (shared minibus) toward the town centre

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~10% at tourist restaurants and for dive/tour guides is appreciated where service isn't already added.
